content.text: Intent
A single self-contained HTML file (markup, CSS and JavaScript inline in one file) that plays a small, funny 2D arcade game:
Cucumber Panic

. The player steers a cat who is terrified of cucumbers; cucumbers rain from the sky and the cat must dodge them while grabbing fish treats. It serves anyone who opens the file in a browser, with no install, server or network. It is a fun, shareable toy.
Scope
IN: one
.html

file holding all markup, styles and scripts; a start screen, the play field, a game-over screen; keyboard and touch control; a score and a best score kept in the browser; drawn graphics and sound made in code.
OUT: external files, libraries, fonts, images or audio files; network access; accounts or online leaderboards; multiplayer; levels or saved progress beyond the best score; server-side persistence.
Scenarios

S1: A player opens the file. The start screen shows the title and a "Press Space or tap to start" prompt. They start, move the cat left and right, dodge cucumbers and catch fish. The cat is hit by a cucumber, loses a life, and shrieks a funny line. After the third hit the game-over screen shows the score and best score; Space or a tap restarts.
Branch: the player pauses with P or Escape, or the browser tab loses focus; the game freezes and resumes on the same key.
Branch: the browser blocks storage; the game still plays and the best score lasts only for the session.
Requirements
R1: The system SHALL be delivered as exactly one HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript inline and no reference to any external resource.

R2: WHEN the player holds the Left or Right arrow key (or A or D), or drags or taps the left or right half of the screen, the system SHALL move the cat in that direction at a constant speed within the play field.

R3: WHILE the game is running, the system SHALL drop cucumbers from the top at random horizontal positions, with the spawn rate rising from 1 per second at score 0 by 1 per second for every 100 points, and the fall speed rising from 200 to 500 pixels per second at the same pace, both capped at 5 per second and 500 pixels per second.
R4: WHEN the cat touches a cucumber, the system SHALL remove that cucumber and take one of the cat's 3 lives.
R5: WHEN the cat touches a fish treat, the system SHALL add 10 points to the score and remove the treat.
R6: WHEN the cat loses its last life, the system SHALL stop play and show the score, the best score and a restart prompt.
R7: WHEN the game ends with a score above the stored best score, the system SHALL store it in the browser as the new best score and show it on the start and game-over screens.
R8: WHEN the player presses P or Escape, or the tab loses focus, while the game is running, the system SHALL pause it; pressing the same key SHALL resume it.
R9: IF browser storage is unavailable, THEN the system SHALL keep playing and hold the best score in memory for the session only.
R10: The system SHALL scale the play field to the browser window while keeping its aspect ratio.
R11: The system SHALL draw all graphics and generate all sounds in code, using no image or audio data from outside the file.
R12: WHEN the player presses M or the on-screen mute button, the system SHALL toggle all sound off or on.

R13: WHILE the game is running, the system SHALL spawn one fish treat every 3 seconds at a random horizontal position at the top, falling at a constant speed, and SHALL remove a treat that reaches the bottom without scoring or costing a life.
R14: WHEN the cat loses a life, the system SHALL show for 2 seconds a speech bubble with a line chosen from a fixed set of at least 5 funny lines, and SHALL play a shriek sound.
R15: WHEN the cat loses a life, the system SHALL make it immune to cucumbers for 1 second, so that overlapping cucumbers cost at most one life in that time.
Data model
None — no persisted business nouns; the only stored value is the best score, held in the browser's own storage.
User interface
None — no root bean, so no designed screen; the game itself is one HTML page with three states (start, play, game-over) and is described by the requirements above.
Dependencies
None — a modern desktop or mobile browser is the only runtime.
Constraints
Performance: the game renders at 60 frames per second on a mid-range laptop with up to 30 cucumbers on screen.
File size: the HTML file is at most 100 KB.
Privacy: nothing is sent over a network; only the best score is stored.
Considered, none apply: authorization, availability, audit, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
A1 (verifies R1): WHEN the file is opened with the network disabled, the system SHALL load and play fully, and the file contains no
src=
or
href=
pointing at an external resource, no
@import
and no
url(
to an external address.

A2 (verifies R2): WHEN the player holds Right for 1 second, the cat's x position increases and stops at the right edge of the play field; the same holds for Left; a tap on the left half moves the cat left.
A3 (verifies R3): WHEN the score is 0, 300 and 1000, the cucumber spawn rate is 1, 4 and 5 per second and the fall speed is 200, 500 and 500 pixels per second respectively.
A4 (verifies R4): WHEN the cat overlaps a cucumber, lives drop by exactly 1 (3 to 2) and the cucumber disappears.
A5 (verifies R5): WHEN the cat overlaps a fish treat, the score rises by exactly 10 and the treat disappears.
A6 (verifies R6): WHEN lives reach 0, play stops and the game-over screen shows the score, the best score and a restart prompt; Space or a tap starts a new game with 3 lives and score 0.
A7 (verifies R7): WHEN a game ends with score 120 and the stored best is 100, the best score becomes 120 and still shows 120 after reloading the page; a game ending with 80 leaves it at 120.
A8 (verifies R8): WHEN P is pressed during play, cucumbers stop moving; pressing P again resumes from the same positions; the same holds for Escape and for tab focus loss.
A9 (verifies R9): WHEN storage access throws an error, the game still starts and plays, and the best score updates for the current session.
A10 (verifies R10): WHEN the window is resized from 1280x720 to 400x800, the play field stays fully visible at its aspect ratio.
A11 (verifies R14): WHEN 20 life losses are simulated, each shows a bubble for 2 seconds with a line from the fixed set of at least 5 lines, and a shriek sound plays unless muted.
A12 (verifies R11): The file contains no
data:
URI, no
, no
<audio>
and no external media reference; graphics appear on a canvas and sound plays through code-generated audio.
A13 (verifies R12): WHEN M is pressed during play, no shriek plays on the next hit; WHEN M is pressed again, it plays on the next hit; the on-screen button does the same.
A14 (verifies R13): WHEN 9 seconds of play pass, exactly 3 fish treats have spawned; a treat that reaches the bottom disappears with the score and lives unchanged.
A15 (verifies R15): WHEN two cucumbers overlap the cat within 1 second of a hit, lives drop by exactly 1 in total; a cucumber touching it after 1 second costs another life.
Migration & compatibility
None — new standalone file, nothing existing to migrate.
Artifacts
None.
Open Questions
None.
